87 years ago, our founders started a new nation on this continent. They built it on freedom. They believed everyone is created equal.

Now we're fighting a civil war. This war will test whether our nation—or any nation built this way—can survive.

You are standing on a major battlefield from that war. We've come to dedicate part of this field as a resting place for the soldiers who died here so our nation could live. This is the right thing to do.

But in truth, we can't make this ground more sacred than it already is. The brave men who fought here, both the living and the dead, have already made it sacred. We can't add to that or take away from it, no matter what we do.

Few people will remember what we say here today. But no one will ever forget what these soldiers did here.

Instead, we the living must finish the work they started. We must commit ourselves to the task still ahead of us.

We should learn from these honored dead. They gave everything for their cause. Their sacrifice should make us more devoted to that same cause.

We must promise that these soldiers did not die for nothing. We must ensure that:

- This nation, under God, will experience a new birth of freedom
- Government of the people, by the people, for the people, will not disappear from the earth
